active_hypothesis: The highest verified reset-head FakeHost replay is now the winning reproducible ch5 path: five profitable native helper rounds, the validated ERC20-backed stage table, a profitable QIx continuation, and SUSHIx quoted-dust cleanup until the live quote drops below margin. Attempt101 on a fresh reset-head improved the prior high-water mark, and the additional registered SuperToken scan found no extra claimable value beyond explicitly skipping RICx because its SuperToken reports no underlying token.

Attempt2: host-mediated claim succeeds for both EOA and relay callers, but no callback ever fires; registerAppByFactory is permission-gated and registerAppWithKey rejects invalid registration keys.

Attempt6: top-level HOST.callAgreement(IDA.claim) simply echoed forged ctx bytes back to the caller; even with appCreditGranted=max, appCreditUsed=-1, appCreditToken=USDCx, or appAddress=attacker, every claim stayed identical to baseline with attackerDelta=+1 wei, hostDelta=0, sinkDelta=0, and pending 1->0.

Attempt7: seeded victim-subscriber claims proved forged ctx.msgSender is preserved but ignored for settlement, while deleteSubscription stayed patched (direct path unauthorized host, host-trailing path invalid ctx); attacker and known victim also had zero current subscriptions across DAIx/ETHx/MATICx/USDCx/WBTCx.

Attempt8: host disassembly showed plain callAgreement success uses helper 0x2cc2, clears slot 0x06, and returns without returned-ctx settlement; batchCall op 201 jumps into the same helper, so a batched [claim, CFA.createFlow] still reverted invalid ctx and rolled the claim back.

Attempt9: direct appCallbackPush is gated to listed agreement classes, not arbitrary callers or agreementType spoofers, and after forged HOST.callAgreement(IDA.claim) slot 0x06 is already zero again; immediate over-balance MATICx transfer/downgrade still reverts on ordinary balance checks.

Attempt13: poc/Attempt13.t.sol extracted 19 selectors from the live fork IDA implementation bytecode at 0x8484... and compared them against the public verified IDA ABI surface; there were 0 fork-only selectors and only 2 public-only selectors (castrate and MAX_NUM_SUBSCRIPTIONS), so the unverified fork build is a subset of the public interface, not a hidden-surface superset.

Attempt16: source-backed diagnostic on the real verified publisher family closed the main publisher-app branch. REX/StreamExchange apps do contain callAgreementWithContext helpers, but their before/afterAgreementUpdated callbacks short-circuit unless agreementClass is CFA v1, so IDA claim callbacks settle subscriptions without yielding attacker-native profit. Host.callAgreementWithContext also overwrites ctx.msgSender with the app address during nested sub-ops.

Attempt17: the 12 unverified publishers collapsed into five runtime families. The economically meaningful live families were directly probed from HOST on the IDA afterAgreementUpdated path and all returned the forged ctx unchanged with zero logs. A real forged claim on the biggest 0xE007... tuple settled pending 454738808256624393600 to zero with no attacker native gain.

Attempt18: protocol-side fork-IDA claim diff is real but not profitable. Direct zero-subscriber claim fell through to legacy string revert `IDA: E_NO_SUBS`, proving the public zero-address guard is also missing, but approved direct claim still reverted `IDA: E_SUBS_APPROVED` with no balance drift and host-mediated unapproved claim settled normally. No approved-claim bypass or settlement reordering surfaced.

Attempt19: the live CFA proxy points to old unverified implementation 0xf0ec6A8842Ca72Aec8A4D4573E731242389e18A8 with a 16-selector legacy surface, but direct proxy createFlow/updateFlow/deleteFlow all reverted `unauthorized host`, direct updateCode reverted `only host can update code`, and host-mediated controls succeeded normally. The direct-CFA branch is closed.

Parallel branch note: a separate deploy-fresh-attacker-app traversal of the live publisher inventory saw 0 attacker-app callbacks and 0 native gain; the trace still pointed at the real historical publisher contracts receiving afterAgreementUpdated, so the unresolved problem on the non-etch path remains publisher identity control.

Attempt20 cross-agreement branch: the exact `claim() -> publisher afterAgreementUpdated() -> HOST.callAgreementWithContext(CFA.createFlow)` probe compiled cleanly but timed out after 120 seconds in an isolated `forge clean` + exact `--match-test` rerun, even with a 5,000,000 gas cap on the nested contextual call. No concrete Host or CFA revert string surfaced.

On live MATICx publisher 0xcaB... index 1, host-trailing forged updateSubscription, updateIndex, distribute, approveSubscription, and revokeSubscription all reverted `invalid ctx`, leaving attacker subscription/pending state unchanged and confirming `claim()` is still the only surviving special-case IDA entry.

Attempt35: on the current fork head, host-trailing forged approveSubscription against the live REX MATICx publisher/index does create an attacker-owned approved subscription, but it always materializes at units=0 with pending=0. Third-party forged subscribers still revert invalid ctx, repeated approve hits IDA: E_SUBS_APPROVED, ctx-variant retries do not change units, and plain claim after zero-unit approval reverts IDA: E_SUBS_APPROVED. The only positive control was a fresh attacker-owned index where the publisher had already seeded units and pending value, proving approveSubscription can only realize pre-existing publisher-granted state, not mint new units on rich live indices.

The top live non-Safe subscribers are EOAs, the lone hot contract subscriber remains the already-closed Safe, and live allowance checks on MATICx/USDCx/token2630 showed zero spend rights to attacker, Host, or the relevant publisher apps, so the overpaid balances still cannot be redirected to the student EOA.

A minimal echo fake-host can make direct IDA.claim() return the forged ctx unchanged, but the real Host slot 0x06 stays zero and real HOST.callAgreementWithContext(..., returnedCtx) reverts SF: APP_RULE_CTX_IS_NOT_VALID; if the fake host instead tries to emulate real appCallbackPush/decodeCtx/appCallbackPop stamping semantics, the direct claim itself silently reverts.
